subject: Climate & Environment
title: Ocean Deoxygenation
description: A quick, practical guide to Ocean Deoxygenation.

hook.text: The ocean is losing oxygen. Dead zones — where nothing can breathe — are expanding fast.

buildup.text: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen than cold water. As oceans heat, oxygen levels drop.

discovery.text: Stronger stratification prevents oxygen-rich surface water from mixing into the deep.

twist.text: The ocean has lost about 2% of its oxygen since the 1960s. Some regions have lost far more.

climax.text: Over 700 dead zones now exist worldwide — up from 45 in the 1960s.

punchline.text: The ocean is suffocating. Most of the world hasn't noticed yet.

quiz.question: Why is the ocean losing oxygen?
options: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen

details.summary: Ocean oxygen levels have dropped about two percent since the 1960s as warmer water holds less dissolved gas and increased stratification reduces mixing. Low-oxygen dead zones expand, suffocating marine life and shrinking habitable ocean space for fish and other organisms.
details.whyItMatters: Deoxygenation threatens fisheries, biodiversity, and the livelihoods of communities that depend on the sea. It amplifies the stress that warming and acidification already place on marine ecosystems.
takeaways: Ocean oxygen has declined roughly two percent since the 1960s
Warmer water physically holds less dissolved oxygen
Expanding dead zones suffocate marine life over large areas

faq.question: What causes ocean dead zones?
faq.answer: Dead zones form when excess nutrients from agricultural runoff fuel algal blooms. As algae die and decompose, bacteria consume oxygen faster than it can be replenished. Climate warming worsens the problem by reducing oxygen solubility and mixing.

faq.question: How does deoxygenation affect fish?
faq.answer: Fish and other aerobic organisms need dissolved oxygen to survive. As oxygen levels drop, habitable zones shrink, forcing species into smaller areas with more competition and less food. Prolonged exposure causes mass die-offs and ecosystem collapse.
